description:
General-purpose 1.7B parameter language model (GGUF), Q8_0 quantised.
This image (Studio's own dev build, `appsork/hutash-inference-cpu`)
runs CPU-only — the published hutash-app pipeline separately declares
a GPU packages.yaml variant for the real, distributed venv install;
see the notes below. Powers the Improve-prompt buttons and
the Prompt Assistant chat panel — "Prompt Improver" is the Settings
feature name, not this model's name. Was invisible, auto-installed
system infrastructure with no model-browser entry; now an ordinary,
user-installable Marketplace model (no auto-install, no UI controls
of its own beyond the two features that call it).
notes: Was invisible infrastructure (internal:true, auto-installed during first-launch onboarding, no model-browser entry). Startup auto-install was removed and Studio overrides internal to false for this id specifically (api/models/catalogue.py's _resolve_pipeline_entry) as a local safety net — the published manifest.yaml (hutash-app's pipelines/prompt-engine.hutash) now also carries internal:false and the real Qwen3 1.7B naming directly, so the override is redundant belt-and- suspenders rather than the only thing keeping this model visible.

GGUF weights fetched at install time (weights-external, not baked into the image) from Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF — the official repo publishes a single Q8_0 quantisation (~1.83 GB); it does not ship a Q4_K_M variant, unlike the unsloth mirror this pipeline used to point at.
Uses Qwen3's `/no_think` sentinel to skip chain-of-thought blocks and save the token budget for the actual response.

The DISTRIBUTED install (hutash-app's pipelines/prompt-engine.hutash, the real venv/pavaka path end users get) is GPU-capable as of that package's own packages.yaml gaining a `gpu:` variant (llama-cpp- python's CUDA wheel index) alongside its existing `cpu:` one, plus a top-level min_vram_gb of 3 there. The engine's `PackageSpec.SelectVariant` (daemon/ext/packages/spec.go) picks GPU automatically whenever a host meets that declared minimum, purely from which variants are declared in that package's packages.yaml. This is unrelated to this file's own `hardware:` block above, which describes Studio's separate CPU-only dev Docker image, not the published pipeline. There is no per-package "compute mode" field (cpu/gpu/any) for a model_pipeline like this one — that concept only exists in Pavaka's app_manager.py, for third-party application installs (ComfyUI etc.).

Container listens on internal port 8000 (universal Aura convention); the host port is assigned dynamically at install time and stored in the model_ports table, like every other model. improver.py resolves it via storage.get_model_port.
